title: Procedure for Decellularization of Rat Livers in an Oscillating-pressure Perfusion Device
protocol: Use a cork plate for fixation.
Put a medical drape on the cork plate.
Fix an inhalation mask on the cork plate using four needles for intraoperative inhalation narcosis.
Connect a peripheral venous catheter (G 20) to a three-way stopcock.
Cut the venous catheter obliquely with a length of approximately 1.5 cm.
De-air the system using a 10 ml syringe filled with Ringer solution.
Use a butterfly cannula and cut the needle to a length of 5 mm.
Fit a 5 cm tube (ID 0.58 mm; OD 0.96 mm) to the 5 mm needle and fix it with superglue.
Insert a 2 cm-long tube (ID 0.28 mm; OD 0.61 mm) into the bigger tube and fix it with superglue.
Slip another tube over this construction as an abutment and fix it with superglue.
De-air the arterial cannula with a 5 ml syringe filled with Ringer solution.
Induce narcosis of the rat in the anesthesia induction chamber by administering 3.5% isoflurane in oxygen at a flow rate of 1.5 L/min.
Inject metamizol at 100 mg/kg body mass intraperitoneally.
Inject ketamine/medetomidine mixture (10 mg/0.1 mg per kg body mass) intraperitoneally.
Supply 1.5% isoflurane in 1 L/min oxygen via the inhalation mask.
Shave the abdomen with an electric shearing machine.
Moisten the shaved incision site on the abdomen with 70% ethanol for disinfection.
Place the animal in the supine position on the prepared plate.
Insert the head into the inhalation mask and fix the limbs with medical tape and pins.
Remove excess ethanol and fur with a gauze compress.
Assess the anesthesia depth by monitoring the respiratory rate.
Check the analgesia level by attempting to trigger the toe pinch reflex using surgical forceps.
Make a median incision in the caudal abdominal wall above the bladder.
Cut from this point to both lateral costal arches in a V-shaped manner, forming a V-shape.
Pull the cut abdominal wall over the chest.
Fix the xiphoid with an overholt clamp and pull it cranially.
Secure the pulled xiphoid with a rubber band.
Evacuate the intestine using wet cotton swabs.
Wrap the intestines in a wet gauze bandage.
Cover all abdominal margins with wet bandages.
Dissect the falciform ligament.
Use a wet gauze bandage to hold the medial and left liver lobes cranially under the dome of the diaphragm.
Expose the hepatoduodenal ligament and the upper omental liver lobe.
Carefully dissect the ligament attached to the upper omental lobe using two microforceps and spring scissors until the lobe is mobile.
Move the upper omental liver lobe using wet cotton swabs under the gauze compress, holding the medial and left lobes in place.
After mobilization of the upper omental liver lobe, move the stomach to the left.
Fix the stomach with a clamp.
Dissect the minor omentum with microforceps and spring scissors.
Mobilize the lower omental liver lobe until it is mobile.
Move the lower omental liver lobe back into its cavity.
Use a Backhaus clamp to retain the duodenum.
Move the duodenum to the left to stretch and expose the hepatoduodenal ligament.
Circumscribe the common bile duct in the stretched hepatoduodenal ligament.
Dissect the bile duct from the adipose and pancreatic tissue.
Cut the bile duct 1.5 cm from the bile duct bifurcation.
Dissect the portal vein from the surrounding adipose tissue.
Expose the gastroduodenal vein.
Ligate the gastroduodenal vein twice with silk 6-0.
Divide the vein between the two ligatures.
Dissect the celiac trunk and the common hepatic artery from the surrounding tissue until all arterial rami are revealed.
Liberate the gastroduodenal artery from the surrounding tissue.
Tie the gastroduodenal artery twice with silk 6-0, with ties distant from each other.
Dissect the gastroduodenal artery between the two ligatures.
Liberate the splenic artery from the surrounding tissue.
Tie the splenic artery twice with silk 6-0, with ties distant from each other.
Dissect the splenic artery between the two ligatures.
Liberate the left gastric artery from the surrounding tissue.
Tie the left gastric artery twice with silk 6-0, with ties distant from each other.
Dissect the left gastric artery between the two ligatures.
Circumscribe the inferior caval vein between the right kidney and the right lateral liver lobe.
Dissect the inferior caval vein from the retroperitoneal space.
Expose the aorta by following the celiac trunk.
Dissect the retroperitoneal adipose tissue.
Inject 1,000 I.E. heparin in 1 ml saline into the inferior vena cava.
Retract the cannula and close the incision with a cotton pad.
Wait 1-2 min for the systemic effect of heparin.
Circumscribe the aorta with forceps.
Dissect the aorta and exsanguinate the rat.
Dissect the inferior vena cava distally from the kidney.
Make a fish-mouth incision in the distal portal vein.
Open the incision with forceps and cannulate the portal vein.
Flush the liver with 20 ml Ringer solution until the liver decolorizes.
Fix the cannula with ligatures (silk 6-0).
Dissect the aorta above the celiac trunk.
Liberate the aorta segment from the retroperitoneal space.
Cut the aorta segment longitudinally to generate an aortic patch.
Insert the self-built cannula into a static holder.
Use 2 forceps to slip the aortic patch over the cannula.
Ligate the hepatic artery with silk 6-0 over the cannula and fix the patch at the abutment.
Open the diaphragm, make a circular incision and dissect the liver from the surrounding structures.
Store the liver in a sterile 500 ml tank filled with 350 ml Ringer solution until use.
Fill a 1,000 ml bottle with 900 ml aqua dest. and add 100 ml Triton X-100 (99.9%).
Use a stirrer to dissolve the Triton X-100.
Fill the bottle with aqua dest. until a total volume of 1,000 ml is reached.
Add 100 ml of the stock solution (10%) to a 1,000 ml bottle.
Add 900 ml aqua dest. and shake the bottle twice.
Filter the 1% Triton X-100 solution through a sterile filter.
Fill a 1,000 ml bottle with 900 ml aqua dest. and add 66.99 g SDS (99.9%, density 0.67).
Use a stirrer to dissolve the SDS.
Fill the bottle with aqua dest. until a total volume of 1,000 ml is reached.
Add 100 ml of the stock solution (10%) to a 1,000 ml bottle.
Add 900 ml aqua dest. and shake the bottle twice.
Filter the 1% SDS solution through a sterile filter.
Link the drain to a three-way stopcock and a Heidelberger extension to regulate the fill level.
Fill the reactor with 500 ml of 0.9% NaCl.
Link the perfusion chamber to the distal end of the bubble trap via the portal venous access or arterial access.
Equip the bubble trap with an obturation at the distal end and a vent.
Connect the bubble trap to a Heidelberger extension.
Link the Heidelberger extension to the pump segment.
Insert another Heidelberger extension into the bottle of detergent solution.
Connect the respirator to the perfusion chamber or pressure distributor for multiple perfusions.
Drain reactor fluids by connecting the outflow to the waste bottle.
Insert the pump segment into the pump.
Start the pump to fill the cycle with PBS.
Close the distal end of the bubble trap and open the vent when filling with PBS.
When the bottom of the bubble is securely covered, close the vent and open the distal end of the bubble trap.
Link the three-way stopcock of the portal vein cannula to the related reactor access.
Connect the arterial cannula to the arterial access carefully avoiding air entry into systems.
Use a respirator with a frequency of 15 bpm and an amplitude of 26 mbar.
Connect the respirator to the pressure distribution chamber.
Connect the chamber to the reactor.
Start pressure application.
Perform perfusion steps with a flow rate of 5 ml/min.
Perfuse the liver with 1% Triton X-100 for 90 min.
Allow waste effluence via the outflow of the perfusion device.
Change the detergent to 1% SDS after 90 min.
